Public claim impacted: CORRECTNESS.md:15 presents a universal equality 'including capacity rejection and the returned packed digest' against a separate specification; CORRECTNESS.md:24 lists 'capacity checking' among the independently connected points.

The independence that is real - the coordinate permutation with LFSR constants regenerated by tools/generate_spec.py (rho recurrence lines 35-37, constants lines 44-52) and the List-based injection/padding walk with the ANode/ALeaf digest tree - does not extend to those four clauses. findings.evidence: RETRACTION EVIDENCE: trusted Base (see trust_boundaries) defines `Array.get.at(-T,i,an) = Array.get.go(T,a,n, U32.and(i, U32.sub(n,1)))` (base.bend:2249-2254) and `Array.size` returns 1 for ALeaf, doubling per ANode (base.bend:2145-2155), so size is a power of two and `i & (size-1)` is exactly `i mod size`; the guide states 'Indexes wrap around.' and that the slot count is a power of two (GUIDE.md:185,188). Hence the reads are total, land on real slots, and cannot trap. PRESERVED OBSERVATIONS: src/keccak.bend:334-336 `sized` is the only gate and checks only `Nat.is_le(length,Nat.mul(4n,U32.to_nat(capacity)))`; src/keccak.bend:312-313 `unchecked` = `blocks(round_count,Nat.div(length,136n),0,Nat.mod(length,136n),...)`; src/keccak.bend:310 advances `index` by 34 per full block; src/keccak.bend:304-305 `finish` -> `pad0` -> ... -> `pad33` each performs an unconditional `Array.get(U32,a,U32.add(index,k))` for k=0..33 (chain verified in src/keccak.bend:168-302); `pad_word(w,pos,remain)` returns 0 for pos>remain and 1 for pos=remain (src/keccak.bend:159-166), discarding the out-of-range reads; spec/sponge.bend:47-58 `gather` issues the same Array.get calls at the same indices; the per-index laws `read33_correct` (proofs/sponge.bend:96-138) and `pad0_correct` (proofs/sponge.bend:2214-2224) carry no size premise because none is needed. CORRECTED ARITHMETIC (this revision): with size = Array.size in slots and 0 <= L <= 4*size, the last index actually consumed is floor((L-1)/4) when L mod 136 != 0 and there are no consumed reads when L mod 136 = 0, so floor((L-1)/4) <= size-1 holds exactly under the guard `L <= 4*size`; the last index issued is q*34+33 with q = floor(L/136), which at L = 4*size equals size-(size mod 34)+33 and exceeds size by 33-(size mod 34) >= 1 for every power-of-two size (2^k mod 34 cycles over {2,4,8,16,18,26,30,32}, all <= 32). The prior report's statements 'reads exceed Array.size only for the smallest rows' and (in the superseded finding) 'sizes 0/32/64/135/136/137 -> size 1' are both wrong and are corrected here. Concrete gate rows (tools/swarm_gate.py:34-36): size 0 -> depth 1 -> 2 slots, L=0, issued reads 0..33 wrap; size 64 -> depth 4 -> 16 slots, L=64, reads 0..33 wrap; size 135 -> depth 6 -> 64 slots, reads 0..33 stay in bounds; size 136 -> 64 slots, L=136, reads 34..67 wrap; size 1024 -> 256 slots, L=1024, reads 238..271 wrap; size 16384 -> 4096 slots, reads 4080..4113 wrap; size 65536 -> 16384 slots, reads 16354..16387 wrap; size 1048576 -> 262144 slots, reads 262140..262173 wrap. In every one of these rows the wrapped reads are discarded because L <= 4*slots. tests/vectors.bend:24 uses depth 7 (128 slots) for all 274 length cases, so those reads are in bounds; the two invalid cases (tests/vectors.bend:32-33, depth 0 with L=5 and depth 7 with L=513) are the capacity-rejection rows.
findings.impact: Retracted: there is no out-of-range access, no trap, and no missing soundness premise; `hash_correct`/`public_correct` are unconditional and hold because production and specification read identical indices, and the guard coincides with the bound that keeps the consumed reads in bounds. Residual facts, all low impact: (i) digest correctness for arrays whose guard-saturating length pushes the issued reads past Array.size depends on Base's index masking and on `pad_word`'s GT branch zeroing the wrapped lanes - a property discharged by pad33_correct..pad0_correct (proofs/sponge.bend:2201-2224 and preceding) but not stated in README.md ('Unused ... trailing array slots are ignored', README.md:62) as an explicit reliance on index wrapping; (ii) ~34 unconditional reads per block, a small constant cost; (iii) the emitted C's faithful realization of the `i & (size-1)` masking is unverified in this review (build/ ignored and absent), and is recorded as a trust boundary rather than a bug.

findings.title: Capacity-rejection refinement is a congruence against a copy of the same predicate, not an independent rejection completeness statement
findings.missing_property: Both directions of rejection over an independently defined capacity: (a) `length > 4*Array.size(a)` implies `keccak256` returns `None` and (b) `length <= 4*Array.size(a)` implies `Some`, with the bound expressed over a specified capacity notion rather than an `Equal.cong` between two syntactically identical predicates.
findings.evidence: proofs/api.bend:117-126 `capacity_gate` states `K.sized(24n,n,(a,capacity)) == None{}` given `invalid : {Nat.is_le(n,Nat.mul(4n,U32.to_nat(capacity))) == False{}}`, and its proof is a pure `Equal.cong(Bool,...)` over the predicate `b => K.checked(24n,b,a,n)`. The production predicate (src/keccak.bend:334-336) and the specification predicate (spec/sponge.bend:78-80) are character-identical, so the theorem restates the implementation's own boolean; the predicate is taken as a hypothesis rather than derived. The direction is nevertheless correct and matches README.md:61, and two invalid-capacity rows are exercised empirically (tests/vectors.bend:32-33: depth 0 with length 5, depth 7 with length 513; expected 'invalid' per tools/validate.py:31-33).
findings.impact: Low: a wrong capacity formula (a factor-of-4 slip, or an off-by-one at `length = 4*size`) would satisfy `capacity_gate` unchanged because the predicate is assumed; nothing in the kernel pins the boundary. The boundary `length = 4*size` is only pinned empirically. Note also that `length = 4*Array.size` is exactly the condition finding 1 shows to be needed for the consumed reads to be in bounds, so the two obligations meet at the same untested equality case.
findings.required_law: `law rejection_complete`: `for a, length, capacity ... {Nat.is_le(length, Nat.mul(4n,U32.to_nat(capacity))) == False{} : Bool} -> K.sized(24n,length,(a,capacity)) == None{}`, plus the acceptance-direction complement, with capacity derived from an independent length model (`Nat.pow(2n,depth)`) rather than the same `Array.size` call, and the boundary equality `length = 4*capacity` as a proof case.
findings.reproduction: Read proofs/api.bend:117-126 beside src/keccak.bend:334-336 and spec/sponge.bend:78-80. DISPROOF: find a theorem that derives the capacity predicate from an independent size model or that case-splits the boundary equality as a proof step rather than a test vector.

findings.title: Failed-operation state: the rejected branch consumes and drops the caller's array, so the documented failure path is destructive and unverified
findings.missing_property: A stated law for the rejection path: what happens to the caller's `Array<U32>` when the capacity check fails (consumed and unrecoverable, or returned/borrowable), and that rejection leaves no observable state behind (no cached result, no partially written digest).
findings.evidence: src/keccak.bend:329-332 `checked` matches `valid`: `False{}` -> `None{}`, `True{}` -> `Some{digest(unchecked(...))}`; in both branches the linear parameter `a` is not returned, so a rejected call consumes the array. src/keccak.bend:334-336 `sized` deconstructs `Array.size(U32,a)` (which threads and returns the array, trusted Base 2150-2155) and passes `a` on. proofs/api.bend:5-11 `rejected` and proofs/sponge.bend:2320-2330 `checked_correct` only relate the `None` result, not the array's fate. README.md:53 and package.bend:7 both say 'Input is consumed', so the behaviour is documented prose, not a law. No `Array.set`/`Array.clone` occurs on the input path before the guard (src/keccak.bend:147-313 is read-only `Array.get`), so rejection cannot leave a partially written input. There is no caching or memoization anywhere in src/ (the digest array is reconstructed per call at src/keccak.bend:315-327) and no mutable global state, so no stale result can be observed across calls: cache invalidation is vacuously satisfied by construction (recorded as a negative result, not a defect).
findings.impact: Low for library consumers: a rejected call destroys the input array in a linear language, so callers must clone before attempting a hash of unknown length, and no theorem (as opposed to a README/package-comment line) promises this. Cache invalidation is genuinely not an issue for this design; the isolation property is satisfied because the output digest is a fresh `Array.new` allocation and the input is only read.
findings.required_law: Either `law rejected_preserves_input` returning the array beside the `Maybe` on failure, or an explicit post-condition (in the law's `def`) that both branches consume the array, matching README.md:53 and package.bend:7.
findings.reproduction: Read src/keccak.bend:329-336 and note neither branch returns `a`; read proofs/api.bend:5-11. DISPROOF: find a rejection-path law in proofs/ that returns or preserves the array.
findings.suggested_fix: Either return the array alongside the `Maybe` on failure, or lift the README.md:53 / package.bend:7 consumption statement into the law's post-condition.
findings.performance_risk: None: the rejection branch is not on the measured path (benchmarks use valid capacities; benchmarks/driver.bend:29 clones explicitly).

findings.title: Public capacity contract bounds only used bytes while the padding traversal performs 34 masked Array.get reads per boundary block, and the accepting boundary length == 4*capacity is never exercised (hazard framing retracted: Base defines get as an index-masking total read)
findings.missing_property: Either the accepted-input domain must bound every element the padding chain actually consumes, or the required semantics of an out-of-range Array.get (Base's index masking) and the fact that every wrapped value at position > remain is discarded by pad_choose must be stated and proved/documented rather than silently relied on; and the acceptance boundary itself must be exercised on the accepting side. Public claim impacted: the documented rule that a byte length is accepted iff it does not exceed four times the array's reported capacity, together with 'unused trailing array slots are ignored' (README:61-62).
findings.evidence: sized (src/keccak.bend:334-336) accepts iff Nat.is_le(length, Nat.mul(4n, U32.to_nat(capacity))), where capacity = Array.size(U32,a) is an element count. blocks (src/keccak.bend:307-310) walks Nat.div(length,136n) full blocks at a 34-word stride (line 310) and finishes the last block by reading 34 consecutive positions: finish (line 304) supplies index and the pad1..pad32 chain (lines 172-302) supplies index+1..index+33 (visible as U32.add(index,33) at line 174 down to U32.add(index,1) at line 302). So the executed read footprint is 34*(floor(length/136)+1) words, while the contract permits capacity as low as length/4 words: 34*(blocks+1) > capacity whenever length/4 <= capacity < 34*floor(length/136)+34, which holds at length == 4*capacity. Concrete instances inside the contract: tests/vectors.bend:30 one(4096n,17,10n) -> capacity 2^10 = 1024 words, blocks = 30, base word 1020, highest index 1053; tests/vectors.bend:31 one(65536n,33,14n) -> highest index 16387 vs 16384; and the frozen gate itself, where swarm_gate.py:34 sets depth = max(0, (((size+3)//4)-1).bit_length()) giving depth 1 for size 0 and capacity 2 words = 8 bytes (swarm_gate.py:15 SIZES[0]=0), so all 34 reads of every empty-input iteration address positions beyond the zero used bytes. Source-supported retraction of the earlier wording: the installed Base defines Array.get as total by construction - Array.get (base.bend:2253-2254) delegates to Array.get.at, which masks the index with U32.and(i, U32.sub(n,1)) (base.bend:2249-2251) before descending, so an index beyond the size aliases into the array (valid because Array.new sizes are powers of two, README:63) instead of trapping or reading unmapped memory. The residual, non-retracted allegation is that this masking plus the discard rule in pad_choose (src/keccak.bend:159-163: GT -> 0, EQ -> 1, LT -> partial) is nowhere stated as a precondition of the public contract; the digest is only correct because wrapped values at pos > remain are multiplied out. The refinement cannot detect a mistake here: spec/sponge.bend:47-58 (gather) mirrors the identical read footprint (33 reads from base+1..base+33 plus a[base]). Acceptance-boundary testing is also one-sided: tests/vectors.bend:32-33 exercise only length>4*capacity rejections (5 bytes/depth 0 and 513 bytes/depth 7) and never length == 4*capacity, which is exactly the maximal-read case. The same shape exists in the public wrapper src/hex.bend:32-33, hex_walk(7n,1,Array.get(U32,a,0)), which consumes 8 positions with no length precondition, so hex of an undersized array silently repeats masked words.
findings.impact: Reduced from the earlier report: with Base's masking there is no memory-safety or trap hazard under the checked-in backend semantics, so this is a contract/specification gap rather than an unsafe read. What remains: (a) the digest's correctness silently depends on a wrap-and-discard interaction that no law, comment or README line states, so a later edit to pad_choose or to the traversal (or a lowering that does not reproduce the masking) is caught only by the empirical suite; (b) the accepting boundary length == 4*capacity - the case where the contract and the read footprint are furthest apart - has no law and no vector; (c) hex inherits the same precondition-free footprint.
findings.required_law: Either a bound law of the form 'length <= 4*Array.size(U32,a) => every position consumed by finish/blocks is discarded-or-in-range under pad_choose', or an explicit statement (CORRECTNESS.md trusted list + README capacity rule) that Base.Array.get masks indices and that pad_choose discards every wrapped word at pos > remain; plus a differential case at the exact boundary length == 4*capacity and one on a 1-word array with a short non-empty message.
findings.reproduction: Statics suffice: compute blocks=floor(length/136) and base=34*blocks from src/keccak.bend:310-312, count the 34 consecutive reads from src/keccak.bend:172-302, and compare with Array.size from src/keccak.bend:339; confirm the masking in the installed Base at base.bend:2249-2254. Disproof of the residual claim would be a checked-in law or README sentence making the masking-plus-discard obligation explicit and a vector at length == 4*capacity.
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer eliminating the reliance: in the padding chain, skip the read when pos >= remain (the value is provably unused) so the footprint becomes proportional to the used bytes, then re-discharge padding_correct/pad*_correct. Otherwise document the masking assumption next to the capacity rule in README/CORRECTNESS.md and in the trusted-components list, and add the two missing differential cases (length == 4*capacity; 1-word array with a short non-empty message). For hex, state or enforce the 8-word precondition.
findings.performance_risk: Removing the unused reads removes up to 33 masked reads per hash boundary block (a small speedup, not a regression); adding two differential cases changes no runtime path. Documenting instead of fixing preserves current timings exactly.

orchestrator.reason: Contract/read-footprint half confirmed (src/keccak.bend:307-313 reads a 34-word window beyond a partially filled block under the masked model). The sub-claim that length == 4*capacity is never exercised is refuted by tests/vectors.bend:30-31 (4096n/17/10n and 65536n/33/14n are exactly length == 4*capacity) and validate.py:31-33, which asserts those rows on both backends.

findings.title: Unreferenced production symbols (generic lane rotation, permutation entry point) lie outside the refinement chain and outside every law
findings.missing_property: Exported modules should not present unproved, unreferenced operations as API, and every public entry point claimed for the permutation should be reachable from the verified chain. Public claims impacted: README:66 that fixed rotations avoid generic rotation calls and that the proof covers the public API.
findings.evidence: src/lane.bend:13-26 defines small/rotate_if/rotate (the generic Nat-shift path); the runtime chain calls only the fixed rol0..rol62 forms (src/permutation.bend round bodies, e.g. src/permutation.bend:44-62) and src/keccak.bend:1-4 imports lane.bend as L but every use is L.xor/L.chi/L.rolN - the generic rotate has no caller in src/, spec/ (which has its own copy at spec/permutation.bend:23-27) or proofs/. src/permutation.bend:210-211 defines permute(s)=rounds(24n,0n,s), but the production entry calls P.rounds directly (src/keccak.bend:170) and LAWS.bend:9-13 constrains rounds, not permute, so no named theorem instantiates permute; spec/permutation.bend defines its own permute as well. small() is only safe for n<=32 (it computes U32.shln(lo,n) with Nat.sub(32n,n)), so the unproved path is also the only precondition-bearing one.

The cost is audit clarity, not a defect in the hash itself.

findings.reproduction: Static: search src/, spec/, proofs/ and LAWS.bend for calls to L.rotate, L.small, L.rotate_if, P.permute and S.permute - the only definitions are the ones cited; the runtime entry uses L.rolN and P.rounds (src/keccak.bend:170, src/permutation.bend:44-62).
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the generic helpers to a clearly internal module (or drop them), and either add the two instantiation laws above or state in CORRECTNESS.md that permute and the generic rotations are unverified surface.

findings.title: The abstract permutation spec is not representation-independent: it imports the production lane/state data types
findings.missing_property: That the specification's state representation (T.Lane as two 32-bit halves with a defined half order, at src/types.bend) is independent of the production representation, so that a representation error cannot be invisible to the refinement.
findings.evidence: tools/generate_spec.py:4 emits the spec header with `import ../src/types.bend as T`, and the generated spec/permutation.bend:2 imports the same module; the committed audit even asserts this import list (tools/validate.py:16-19). The spec's xor/chi/rotate_small and at/rounds all operate on T.W/T.S, i.e. the production constructors, so lane half ordering, the W{lo,hi} convention and the S{25 lanes} shape are shared by construction. The mechanism is the same one that makes spec/sponge.bend's padding clauses definitional, but here it reaches the only genuinely independent layer (the coordinate round function), because the rounds are stated over production lanes and the 'independent' LFSR round constants are placed into T.W pairs.
findings.impact: A wrong lane representation or half ordering in src/types.bend would be reproduced identically on both sides of the refinement, so Q.rounds_correct would still hold and the permutation half of the correctness argument would be silent about it. The doc-level claim of an independent permutation specification is weaker than it reads.
findings.required_law: A representation-level obligation (or an explicit statement that the abstract model shares src/types.bend and that representation errors are outside the refinement): e.g. a law relating the specification's lane abstraction to an independently defined bitstring/byte vector, or a documented trust boundary in CORRECTNESS.md naming src/types.bend as shared and unverified by the refinement.
findings.reproduction: Read tools/generate_spec.py:4 and spec/permutation.bend:1-2; confirm both import ../src/types.bend as T; then inspect src/types.bend's W{lo,hi} convention and observe that spec/permutation.bend's rotate/xor/chi are defined over the same constructors.
findings.suggested_fix: In scope (proofs/ and docs are editable; spec/ and tools/ are protected, so the generated spec itself cannot be regenerated): state the sharing explicitly in CORRECTNESS.md's independence section and add a proofs/-side lemma or remark that the spec is representation-shared, so readers do not treat Q.rounds_correct as independent of src/types.bend. If a truly independent model is desired it must be generated as a new proof-side module, which is beyond the editable scope and should be recorded as a limitation.
findings.performance_risk: None: documentation and proof-side statements only; no src/ arithmetic or benchmark path is touched.

findings.title: The frozen benchmark gate's anti-elision checksum is a 32-bit function of digest word 0 only
findings.missing_property: That the timed Bend binary in build/swarm-bench actually computes the full 32-byte Keccak-256 digest (i.e. that no optimisation has elided words 1-7 of the output) before its timings are accepted as representative of the original workload.
findings.evidence: tools/swarm_gate.py:39 derives the expected value from digest[:4] (the first four bytes) multiplied by the iteration count, and line 46 accepts the run when lines[1] equals it; benchmarks/driver.bend:10 folds over Array.get(U32,a,0) only, printing a single word. The full-digest checksum exists for the other backends and for Bend through a different executable (tools/benchmark_all.py:19 for c_optimized/c_portable/Lean, and 27-28 for Bend via build/vectors), so the anti-elision guard on the timed binary is 32 bits derived from one word.
findings.impact: The timed gate would accept a compiled binary whose access to digest words 1-7 was removed, because the checksum never depends on them; the timing would still be published as Keccak-256 throughput. Digest-word correctness is independently protected by the separate vectors gate (which compares the full 64-hex-char digest), so this is a benchmark-assurance defect rather than a soundness hole in the proof.
findings.required_law: Not a Bend law: the requirement is that the timed check be a function of the full 32-byte digest (or that an explicit, machine-checked statement record that DCE of words 1-7 is impossible and that the benchmark measures the unelided computation).
findings.reproduction: Run tools/swarm_gate.py benchmark; observe line 39/46 compute and compare a single 32-bit value derived from digest[:4]; read benchmarks/driver.bend:10 and confirm only word 0 is folded and printed.
findings.suggested_fix: Out of editable scope (tools/ is protected). Record in README.md/CORRECTNESS.md that the timed checksum covers digest word 0 only and that full-digest equality is established by the separate vectors gate, and note that DCE exclusion for words 1-7 is unproved. Do not edit tools/swarm_gate.py or benchmarks/driver.bend.
findings.performance_risk: None for the repair; a future in-scope-free change that strengthened the checksum to 8 words would add one fold per iteration and is therefore not recommended inside the frozen workload.

findings.title: The specification's total fallbacks (zero lane, zero constant) hide coordinate or index errors instead of rejecting them

locations.symbol: def at(s: T.State, i: Nat) -> T.Lane ... case _ _: T.W{0,0}
def constant(i: Nat) -> T.Lane ... case _: T.W{0,0}

findings.missing_property: That an out-of-range coordinate or round index in the specification is an error rather than a silently neutral value, so that the refinement is sensitive to indexing mistakes on either side.
findings.evidence: tools/generate_spec.py:31-33 generates `at` with a catch-all `case _ _: T.W{0,0}`, and line 51-53 generates `constant` with `case _: T.W{0,0}`. Any index outside 0..24 or outside the 24 generated constants therefore yields a defined zero value. Since spec/sponge.bend (protected, and itself the counterpart of the production side) is checked against this spec, an indexing discrepancy that lands on a fallback row would be absorbed rather than refuted. I did not exhibit such a discrepancy; the observation is that the spec's totality removes a class of counterexamples.
findings.impact: Weakens the spec's ability to act as an independent oracle for index-coordinate mistakes in the permutation; no demonstrated wrong behaviour follows, and the production side is separately exercised by 278 differential vectors on two backends.
findings.required_law: A specification-side invariant that all accessed coordinates lie in range (equivalently, non-total `at`/`constant` with a refutation on out-of-range indices), or an explicit note that the model is total by construction.
findings.reproduction: Read tools/generate_spec.py:31-33 and 51-53, then read spec/permutation.bend's generated at/constant and confirm the `case _ _: T.W{0,0}` / `case _: T.W{0,0}` fallbacks exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Out of editable scope (spec/ and tools/ are protected). Document in CORRECTNESS.md that the specification is total, i.e. that out-of-range coordinates and round indices return zero in the model, and that the model is therefore not an error-detector for coordinate indexing.
